- Availability and negativity biases: vivid, dramatic events (terror attacks, mass shootings, pandemics) get far more attention and stick in memory, making them seem more frequent.
- Media and social media amplify unusual, alarming stories and make them highly salient across time and space.
- Better reporting and global news coverage can make problems seem new or more widespread even when underlying rates are stable or declining.
